paragraphs.source_en: My master's wife has her backside turned toward him. What is that you say? That such a wife is shockingly improper? There is nothing improper about it. Whether something is proper or improper depends entirely on how the parties interpret it. My master calmly rests his chin beside his wife's backside, and she, just as calmly, sits with that solemn backside planted directly before his face; that is all, and propriety does not enter into it. Within less than a year after their marriage, the two had already become a detached sort of couple, liberated from a marital relation in which etiquette and the like made them constrain each other. Well then, what can she be thinking now, with her backside turned toward my master? Taking advantage of this fine weather, she has scrubbed her more-than-a-foot-long, green-cloud-like black hair with seaweed paste and raw egg, then tossed the smooth strands ostentatiously from her shoulders down her back, and in silence is earnestly sewing a child's sleeveless jacket. In truth, it was to dry this washed hair that she had brought a muslin cushion and her sewing box out to the veranda, and reverently turned her backside toward my master. Or perhaps it was my master who deliberately brought his face around to the quarter where the backside was. At that moment, the smoke I mentioned a little while ago was drifting to and fro through his wife's luxuriant black hair, and my master was absorbed in watching this unexpected, shimmering wisp like an out-of-season heat haze. Smoke, however, does not remain still; by its very nature it is always rising upward. If my master's eyes were to keep watching this strange spectacle of smoke tangling with hair, he had no choice but to keep moving his gaze. My master began his observation around his wife's waist, then slowly followed her spine upward to her shoulders and the nape of her neck; when he passed beyond that and at last reached the crown of her head, he was startled to find a large, perfectly round bald patch in the very middle of the head of the lady with whom he had sworn to share old age and the grave. Moreover, that bald patch was reflecting the warm sunlight and shining. Having made this strange great discovery in such an unexpected place, my master's half-closed eyes in the sunlight immediately showed full astonishment, and, heedless of the dazzling glare, he opened them wide and stared fixedly. When my master saw this bald patch, the first thing that rose in his mind was the oil-lamp dish that for generations had adorned the family Buddhist altar. His family belonged to the Shin sect, and in that sect it had long been the custom to spend on Buddhist altars beyond one's station; my master remembered that when he was small, in the family's storehouse, there stood in the dimness a shrine thickly covered with gold leaf, and inside it a brass lamp dish was always hanging, its dull flame burning even by day. Because the surroundings were dark while this lamp dish shone with comparative brightness, the bald patch on his wife suddenly called up the old impression, seen countless times in his childish heart. The image of the lamp dish vanished from his mind in less than a minute. This time he suddenly remembered the pigeons at the Kannon Hall.

units.source_en: My master's wife has her backside turned toward him. What is that you say?
units.source_zh: 主人的妻子正把屁股对着主人，您说什么？

units.source_en: That such a wife is shockingly improper? There is nothing improper about it.
units.source_zh: 这样的妻子太不成体统了，这没什么。

units.source_en: Within less than a year after their marriage, the two had already become a detached sort of couple, liberated from a marital relation in which etiquette and the like made them constrain each other.

units.source_en: Well then, what can she be thinking now, with her backside turned toward my master?
units.source_zh: 那么，现在她把屁股朝向主人，不知在想什么。

units.source_en: Taking advantage of this fine weather, she has scrubbed her more-than-a-foot-long, green-cloud-like black hair with seaweed paste and raw egg, then tossed the smooth strands ostentatiously from her shoulders down her back, and in silence is earnestly sewing a child's sleeveless jacket.
units.source_zh: 她利用这样的好天气，把一尺多长的绿云一般的黑发用海藻和生鸡蛋哗啦哗啦地洗过，并把理顺的头发潇洒地从肩头披散到后背上，一声不响地专心缝制小孩的坎肩。

units.source_en: In truth, it was to dry this washed hair that she had brought a muslin cushion and her sewing box out to the veranda, and reverently turned her backside toward my master.
units.source_zh: 其实，她是为了吹干她的头发，所以才把毛斯林坐垫和针线盒拿到廊子里来，毕恭毕敬地把屁股朝向主人的。

units.source_en: Moreover, that bald patch was reflecting the warm sunlight and shining.

units.source_zh: 主人在意想不到的地方获得这一奇怪的大发现，他那在阳光下半睁半闭的眼睛，立即显示出惊奇的神色，并且不顾耀眼的强光，一味睁大眼睛，目不转睛地瞧着。

units.source_en: When my master saw this bald patch, the first thing that rose in his mind was the oil-lamp dish that for generations had adorned the family Buddhist altar.
units.source_zh: 当主人看到这块秃点时，首先浮现在他脑海里的是几辈子都设在传家佛龛上的油灯盏子。

units.source_en: Because the surroundings were dark while this lamp dish shone with comparative brightness, the bald patch on his wife suddenly called up the old impression, seen countless times in his childish heart.

units.source_en: The image of the lamp dish vanished from his mind in less than a minute.

units.source_zh: 这回他突然回想起观音堂的鸽子来。

paragraphs.source_en: The pigeons at the Kannon Hall and the bald patch on his wife's crown seem to have no relation whatever, yet in my master's mind they stirred up an intimate association. This, too, dated from my master's childhood: whenever he went to the Kannon Hall at Asakusa, he would always buy beans to feed the pigeons; one small dish of beans cost two Bunkyu coins and came in a reddish earthenware saucer. That earthen saucer, in both color and size, closely resembled his wife's bald patch.
